assessment: The university assessment guide explains how coursework is submitted and how deadlines are handled. Students should upload the final assignment through the learning portal before the deadline shown on the course page. The portal accepts PDF files for the final submission unless the course instructor publishes a different format instruction. Students should keep the upload receipt until the grade is released. Late submission is normally penalized. Illness extensions require medical evidence submitted to the course coordinator before the deadline. The evidence must identify the period of illness, but students should not place unnecessary private medical details in a public discussion forum. A request is reviewed by the coordinator and is not automatically approved. A student who cannot access the portal should contact the help desk before the deadline and keep a screenshot of the error. The help desk can record a technical incident, but it cannot approve an academic extension. Group assignments should be uploaded by the nominated group representative. Each group member remains responsible for checking that the correct file appears in the portal. A file name should include the course code and student identifier, but public examples must use fictional identifiers. Students should not share login passwords with classmates. These instructions are synthetic teaching data and are not an actual university policy.
it_help: The IT help guide covers account access, passwords, recovery codes and support requests. A forgotten password can be reset using the recovery link on the sign in page. The student should open the link from the registered email address and follow the instructions displayed by the identity service. If the recovery email does not arrive, check the spam folder and confirm that the registered address is still accessible. Never share recovery codes with another person or paste them into a public chat. If the account is locked after repeated attempts, wait for the lock period to end or contact the IT help desk for identity verification. The help desk may ask for a student number through its approved private channel, but it will never ask for the current password. Multi factor authentication prompts should be approved only when the student is actively signing in. Unexpected prompts should be denied and reported. A student who loses access to a registered phone should request an account recovery review. Staff must verify identity before changing account recovery settings. Password reset instructions do not restore deleted coursework or change course enrollment. Students should keep personal recovery information private and remove credentials from screenshots before sharing an issue. These steps are fictional examples prepared for this lab.
returns: The parcel support guide explains what a customer should do when an order arrives damaged, delayed or incomplete. For a damaged parcel, contact support within 48 hours and attach photographs of the item and packaging. Keep the shipping label until the report has been reviewed. The photographs should show the damage clearly and should not include unrelated personal documents. Support staff record the order reference and may request one additional image if the first images do not show the affected area. A report submitted after the stated window may need manual review and is not guaranteed to qualify for a replacement. The 48 hour window applies to the synthetic PK region rule in this document. A separate example for another region uses a 72 hour reporting window, so region metadata must be checked before giving guidance. For a change of mind, return unused items within 14 days in their original packaging. This change of mind period is not the damaged parcel reporting period. Missing items should be reported with a photograph of the parcel contents and the packing slip. Customers should not send payment card numbers or account passwords to support. The guide is a fictional dataset for retrieval testing, not a real retailer policy or legal promise.
workplace: The workplace guide describes remote work eligibility for employees and contractors. Employees may request remote work with manager approval. The request should state the proposed work location, expected schedule and contact method during working hours. Approval depends on role requirements, information security and team coverage. Contractors may work remotely only when the signed contract explicitly permits remote work. A manager's informal message does not replace a missing contract condition. Contractor arrangements must be checked against the signed contract and the applicable project statement. Employee remote work rules do not automatically apply to contractors. Staff should use approved devices and protect confidential documents when working away from the office. Public Wi Fi should not be used for confidential work unless the approved secure connection is active. A remote work request may be refused when the role requires on site equipment or controlled access. Changes to work location should be recorded with the responsible manager. The guide also explains that flexible hours and remote location are separate permissions. A person may have approval for one and not the other. All examples in this file are synthetic and do not describe an actual employer's policy. When two passages appear to conflict, check the audience, document date and signed agreement before drawing a conclusion.
printer: The equipment guide contains troubleshooting steps for common printer and scanner problems. For blank printer pages: 1. Check ink level. 2. Run the printer cleaning utility. 3. Print a test page. Follow the device manual. Do not open the printer casing while it is connected to power. If the test page remains blank, confirm that the selected printer matches the physical device and check whether the cartridge protective strip was removed. A low ink warning may appear before the page becomes completely blank. The cleaning utility can use ink, so it should not be repeated many times without checking the device instructions. A blank scanner image is a different problem. Check document placement and select the correct scanning source. Do not apply printer cleaning steps to a scanner. Record the device model and operating system when contacting technical support. If paper is jammed, turn the device off and follow the manufacturer's safe removal instructions. Never pull hard on a sheet that is caught inside moving parts. The sequence of numbered steps matters because later checks depend on earlier ones. During a fault review, a technician should record the printer model, the exact warning shown, the order in which checks were attempted, whether the test page changed after cleaning, and whether the same blank output occurred from another computer before deciding that a cartridge or internal component has failed. This is synthetic training content. It does not replace the manufacturer's manual or a technician's safety advice.
